newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Dlr/mark may gain from rising yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Dlr/mark may gain from rising yen.

text.p: Dollar/mark may find additional help from a rising yen that is pounding a mark already weakened by uncertainty about the European Monetary Union (EMU), analysts said on Wednesday.
Mark/yen on Wednesday violated strong support at 65.20, a 62-percent retracement from the low of 58.70 set in April 1995 to the high of 75.87 in November 1996, they also said.
"The risk is 64.00 the figure," cautioned I.D.E.A. analyst Ben Morden.
In late afternoon trading, mark/yen was quoted at 64.83, just above a session's low at 64.69.
George Tzanetatos, a vice president with Merrill Lynch, agreed "the momentum is still powerful for the yen and it does not let go."

"Mark/yen is moving on momentum. If the yen goes for another big boost up, we'll probably trade completely below 65.00, not just marginally below," Tzanetatos said. "Mark/yen is probably going to continue to erode. Medium term, I see even 60.00 yen to the mark."
Tzanetatos saw the yen rising against the dollar and "go through the 110 level, the bottom of the 114.00- to 110.00 current range."
Technical analysts noted that, unlike in 1995 when the dollar set record lows against both the mark and the yen, the U.S. currency this time was pressured only by the yen.
"Dollar/mark is consolidating. It's going sideways," added Tzanetatos who expected dollar/mark to keep on trading between the May 12 low of 1.6680 and the June 6 high of 1.7423.

Chartists said the fact dollar/mark set a higher recent low just above 1.7080 pointed to an attack on 1.7215, the 62-percent retracement of the move from the 39-month high set at 1.7423 to Wednesday's low. The 1.7080 level now is key support for dollar/mark, they added.
Mark/Paris remained another cross bearing watching as it move closer to a retest of key resistance at 3.3835 amid doubts about the EMU.
The June 2 peak of 3.3865 appears still vulnerable and, if taken out, it would point to an upward move with 3.4015 as the target, chartists also said.

In another display of yen's strength, Swiss/yen retreated under 77.70, paving the way for a test of major support at 75.75 -- the 62-percent retracement of the move from August 1993 to November 1995, chartists at MCM CurrencyWatch said.
